coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K02. Employers of household staff must report entries/exits within 10 days after month-end to the AHV-IV-FAK, the Ausländer- und Passamt and the Amt für Statistik (statistikportal.li Wegleitung Einzelmeldung). A 2017 Volksblatt item (ahv.li press archive) says direct hiring is more complicated than in AT/CH and the government wanted to simplify it. I found no Liechtenstein equivalent of the Swiss simplified accounting procedure, and could not confirm whether any reform was implemented.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Budget; no search run. Likely tiny market.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Budget; no search run.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Only one search, on SPG dealer coverage. Could not confirm whether precious-metal dealers or cash thresholds are in Art. 3 SPG. The SPG was amended in December 2024 (LGBl. 2025 Nr. 101). Unverified.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Budget; no search run.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: The Amt für Lebensmittelkontrolle und Veterinärwesen enforces the Tierseuchenpolizeigesetz and livestock-trade rules. Cattle, sheep, goat, pig and equid identification and registration follow the Swiss Tierverkehrsdatenbank by treaty (customs union of 1923). That is a Swiss-run system, so a local tool is unlikely to be needed. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Budget; no search run.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Budget; no search run.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Budget; no search run. Animal health falls under the same Swiss-treaty regime as category 6.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Budget; no search run.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Budget; no search run.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Only the tank-installation angle was searched (see 37). The Amt für Umwelt does 'Vollzug im Bereich Tankanlagen' (monitoring, permits, inspections) per a Landesverwaltung job posting. Intervals and owner duties unconfirmed, and Swiss rules probably apply by treaty. Lifts and boilers not searched.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Budget; no search run.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Budget; no search run.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Covered under 26. The Arbeitsvermittlungsgesetz of 12 April 2000 (LGBl. 2000 Nr. 103) and the AVV (LGBl. 2000 Nr. 146) require a permit from the Amt für Volkswirtschaft. A Swiss permit is a prerequisite. The CH-FL reciprocity agreement is in force since 1 April 2010. The responsible manager must be a CH or LI citizen, and a security deposit is required. Very few operators. Nothing new for software.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Budget; no search run.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Strong finding: the PGR reform of the law on associations (LGBl. 2024 Nr. 370, in force 1 January 2025) makes charitable associations subject to commercial-register entry (Art. 247 para. 2 PGR, Art. 92 HRV) unless the Amt für Justiz grants an exemption. Associations that existed on 1 January 2025 had until 30 June 2026 (now passed). Registered associations must have a domestic Repräsentanz and a board member meeting Art. 180a PGR unless all payments go through LI/EEA/CH accounts. They must keep a Mitgliederverzeichnis in Liechtenstein and report beneficial owners under the VwbPG. I found no software or vendor aimed at this. See candidate.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Road transport firms need a permit from the Amt für Volkswirtschaft under the Strassentransportgesetz (LGBl. 2006 Nr. 185, 2019 version names the AVW). Taxi drivers need a Zulassungskarte from the Amt für Strassenverkehr (valid 24 months, not renewable). There are few operators. The 2024 amendment of the Entsendegesetz (LGBl. 2024 Nr. 494 and 498 appear in results; the numbers are unconfirmed) adds posting rules for road-transport drivers, with Landespolizei roadside checks. See candidate on cross-border notification.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Budget; no search run.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools: the Fahrlehrerverordnung (LGBl. 741.54) gives permits through the Amt für Strassenverkehr for CHF 100, with inspection fees (Art. 23). The market is tiny. Nurseries and childminders: the Amt für Soziale Dienste approves them under the KJG (LGBl. 2008 Nr. 29) and the Kinderbetreuungsverordnung. Day parents working more than 40 paid hours a month need approval, and most are placed by the Eltern-Kind-Forum. Parents' state subsidy under the KBBV is a separate matter. Tattoo, food and hunting not searched.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Budget; only a tank-owner search was run (see 12 and 37).

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: No commodity trade or milling sector of any size in a landlocked microstate of about 40,000 people.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Budget; no search run.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Liechtenstein adopted the Swiss TARDOC and Ambulante Pauschalen tariffs through the Krankenversicherungsverordnung amendment of 2 December 2025 (LGBl. 2025 Nr. 553). Billing is either TARDOC or flat rates, never mixed. The Ärztekammer assigns Dignitäten. The switch is already done and Swiss practice-management software vendors cover it. Substitution-treatment doctors must report annually to the Amt für Gesundheit. See weak candidate.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: The Betäubungsmittelgesetz requires a permit from the Amt für Gesundheit for narcotics handling. The Heilmittelgesetz (812.102) applies to retail sale, and self-made medicines must be notified to the Amt für Gesundheit (10-year confirmation). I found no Liechtenstein bookkeeping rule or pharmacy-specific duty. Pharmacy count unknown but small. Nothing promising.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Personalverleih and Arbeitsvermittlung need an LI permit that depends on a Swiss permit. Deposit and reciprocity apply, and the market is very small. Security and cleaning not searched.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: The relevant duty is the Entsendegesetz notification for foreign contractors, plus a ZPK report in sectors with generally binding collective agreements. See candidate. No site register was found.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: One search. The SPG (LR 952.1) and SPV cover due-diligence duties and were amended in December 2024 and early 2025. I could not confirm whether real-estate brokers or dealers in goods are covered or who supervises them. Unverified. Related to K01 but a different buyer.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Two searches, no Liechtenstein-specific rule found. The Gewerbegesetz (LGBl. 2020 Nr. 415) with the Gewerbeverordnung (15 December 2020) and the hospitality qualification ordinance cover the permit. I could not confirm a guest register or tourist levy in Liechtenstein. Unverified, so mark as nothing found.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Budget; no search run. Customs union with Switzerland means Swiss customs rules apply.

coverage.category: 31. Cross-border service providers and posted workers (Entsendegesetz and Gewerbegesetz notification)
coverage.found: The Entsendegesetz (LGBl. 2000 Nr. 88) Art. 6a requires the sending employer, and the domestic client if it is a business, to report to the Amt für Volkswirtschaft. Providers from EU/EEA/CH need an annual online confirmation before starting work (IHK Konstanz). There is a ZPK report where collective agreements apply, and foreign firms must register for VAT with the Steuerverwaltung. The act was amended on 8 November 2024 and the Entsendeverordnung on 26 November 2024 (road transport). See candidate.

coverage.category: 32. Trade licensing: Gewerberegister, registrations and permits (Gewerbegesetz 2020)
coverage.found: Every commercial activity needs a Gewerbeberechtigung, either a simple registration or a permit (Annex 1 GewV). Requirements include a domestic delivery address, a domestic establishment with staff (Art. 16) and a legal representative (Art. 17). The Amt für Volkswirtschaft keeps the register and supervises. A draft amendment to the Gewerbegesetz was out for consultation (llv.li srk file). A service for foreign firms needing a domestic address or establishment could be a niche, but it is not a recurring filing. Weak.

coverage.category: 33. Associations and foundations under the PGR reform 2025 (VwbPG, Repräsentanz, Mitgliederverzeichnis)
coverage.found: See 17. For foundations, board members must file registration and confirm the beneficiary class. Most of that belongs to the TCSP world (K01).

coverage.category: 34. Medical tariff change TARDOC (Krankenversicherungsverordnung, LGBl. 2025 Nr. 553)
coverage.found: See 24. Already live since 1 January 2026.

coverage.category: 35. Energy: photovoltaic self-consumption, ZEV and feed-in (Energieeffizienzgesetz, LKW)
coverage.found: The 2022 government report (BuA 79/2022) covers minimum remuneration for PV, Eigenverbrauch and ZEV. PV output in 2025 was 70,681 MWh, up 21.7% on 2024. I could not confirm any owner reporting duty. The state utility LKW is the counterparty. Unverified and weak.

coverage.category: 36. Weapons dealers and holders (Waffengesetz LGBl. 2008 Nr. 275, WaffV LGBl. 2009 Nr. 166)
coverage.found: The Landespolizei keeps the weapons register. Transfer contracts must be kept for 10 years and buyer identity checked. A dealer permit exists with exam and issuing fees. A 2026 Landtag interpellation answer (BuA 15/2026) names safe storage as a gap in the rules. Only a handful of dealers, so tiny.

coverage.category: 37. Tank installations and heating-oil tanks (Amt für Umwelt)
coverage.found: The Amt für Umwelt supervises. I could not find LI inspection intervals or owner duties. Swiss cantons require inspection every 10 years for controlled tanks, and Swiss water-protection law probably applies by treaty, but that is unconfirmed. Unverified.

coverage.category: 38. Monthly employee entry/exit report (Meldung von Beschäftigten, Amt für Statistik / AHV-IV-FAK / AuPA)
coverage.found: Every employer, including households, must report entries and exits within 10 days after month-end. Ordinary payroll software or the portal already handles it. It is relevant only as part of K02.

candidates.buyer: Owners of permit-required tank installations (heating-oil, diesel, businesses, farms, and the approved inspection firms and oil suppliers)
candidates.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors (also touches 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors)
candidates.evidence: https://www.llv.li/en/individuals/recreational-environmental-and-animal-management/water-water-ecology/tank-systems (seen only as a search snippet; direct fetch returned 403). VWF text not opened. LGBl. numbers from the same search: gesetze.li/konso/pdf/2008245000 and /2010020000 (may be the VWF; unconfirmed).
candidates.existing: None seen. The tank control book is a physical paper book issued by the Amt für Umwelt. Swiss tank-inspection software was not searched.
candidates.name: Tank control book and 10-year inspection tracker for oil and fuel tank owners (VWF)
candidates.trigger: Verordnung über den Schutz der Gewässer vor wassergefährdenden Flüssigkeiten (VWF), enforced by the Amt für Umwelt: inspections of permit-required installations every 10 years by approved firms. Leak-detector function checks every 1 or 2 years. Every installation needs a Tankkontrollbuch, and suppliers may not fill an installation without it. Changes and incidents must be reported. A lost book costs CHF 30 to replace.
candidates.unchecked: Number of permit-required installations (likely a few hundred to low thousands); whether the Amt für Umwelt has an online notification or the approved inspection firms already use their own software; whether Swiss tank software (e.g. cantonal tank registers) covers Liechtenstein; whether oil-heating phase-out is shrinking the base. No competitor search run (score below 3).

candidates.buyer: Liechtenstein beekeepers' association and its members (roughly a few hundred keepers, not counted)
candidates.existing: The ALKVW and the beekeepers' association already maintain the register jointly. Swiss beekeeping forms (BLV Bestandeskontrolle Bienenvölker) are available. No software product searched.
candidates.name: Beekeeper apiary register, movement notice and treatment journal
candidates.trigger: Bienenseuchenverordnung, Tierseuchenverordnung and Feuerbrandverordnung: apiary registration with coordinates, advance notice of colony moves to both bee inspectors, and a veterinary-medicine treatment journal.
candidates.unchecked: Number of beekeepers; whether the association offers an app or digital register; willingness to pay is likely near zero.

candidates.evidence: https://www.gesetze.li/chrono/pdf/2024373000, https://www.gesetze.li/chrono/pdf/2024370000 and https://www.gesetze.li/chrono/pdf/2024017000 (from search snippets; texts not opened). Register search at handelsregister.li.
candidates.existing: Not searched. Likely lawyers and Treuhänder handle it. Close to K01 in theme (compliance tracker) but a different buyer group.
candidates.name: Association and cooperative Handelsregister registration and audit-waiver compliance (PGR changes from 1 Jan 2025)
candidates.trigger: Amended PGR (Art. 247 para. 2, Art. 192, Art. 1058a) and Handelsregisterverordnung Art. 92 from 1 Jan 2025: registration and auditor requirement when an association runs a commercial business, is subject to audit, or mainly collects or distributes assets for charity. Member-list duty where members carry liability or extra contributions (Art. 461 ff., 468 ff.). Amt für Justiz examines filings.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the 2025 change created a one-off deadline for many associations; how many associations are affected; competitor check. The category belongs to another worker, listed as a stray find.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No Liechtenstein-specific scrap-dealer licence or register found. Only the general Abfallgesetz 1988 and Altfahrzeugverordnung (AFV, LGBl. 2004 Nr. 153) turned up. The country is tiny and has no known scrap-register regime. Nothing new beyond general waste law.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Liechtenstein pawnbroker or second-hand-dealer regime found. Only the Gewerbegesetz general licensing (Amt für Volkswirtschaft) and the itinerant-trade law and ordinance (LGBl. 2004 Nr. 12, gesetze.li/konso/pdf/2004012000) appeared. Pawnbroking in neighbouring Switzerland is cantonal, so a Swiss rule may not apply. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Altfahrzeugverordnung AFV (LGBl. 2004 Nr. 153, amended LGBl. 2014 Nr. 263): holders must hand end-of-life vehicles to a disposal facility, with free take-back and an advance disposal fee collected by the Motorfahrzeugkontrolle. Disposal facilities need a permit under the Abfallgesetz (Art. 22 with Art. 14). Operators are very few; a Swiss association (VASSO) reportedly also represents Liechtenstein collection points. No candidate; the buyer pool is a handful.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Food control is under the Lebensmittelkontrollverordnung LMKV (16 May 2000) and Swiss-aligned food law, run by ALKVW. Butchers and slaughter operators must keep documented self-control (HACCP). Only Swiss and German templates appeared and no Liechtenstein-specific portal or form was found. Very few operators. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Per llv.li search snippet: ALKVW with the Liechtenstein beekeepers' association records all apiaries (keeper names, colony counts, coordinates). Apiary moves outside the home inspection district must be reported beforehand to both bee inspectors. Beekeepers also keep a veterinary-medicine treatment journal. Inspections are association-run. Laws: Bienenseuchenverordnung, Tierseuchenverordnung, Feuerbrandverordnung. The association and ALKVW already hold the register, and the buyer pool is tiny. Weak candidate listed. The llv.li page itself was blocked (403).

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Tierärztegesetz (LGBl. 2009 Nr. 6, LR 811.13) exists. Animal-medicine rules follow the EEA/Swiss framework. No Liechtenstein-specific vet-reporting portal or distinct duty found. Swiss vet practice software is likely to serve the few practices. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Wasserrechtsgesetz 1979 and its ordinance: abstraction installations on public waters must be notified to the Amt für Umwelt before construction. Verliehene Wassernutzungen pay an annual Wasserzins, assessed on abstracted volume by meter or pump rating. Gewässerschutzgesetz 2003 has groundwater protection zones. Very few operators; no quiet recurring register for small firms found.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Gewässerschutzverordnung (LGBl. 1997 Nr. 42) covers wastewater. Liechtenstein is nearly fully sewered, so the septic-emptying market is negligible. No emptying-log rule found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Water supply is run mainly by municipal utilities and the WLU (Wasserversorgung Liechtensteiner Unterland). Self-control for drinking water follows Swiss-style HACCP templates (found only for Graubünden, as a comparison). No small private water-system register in Liechtenstein was found. Buyers would be a handful of municipal utilities.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Per llv.li search snippets: Liechtenstein applies Swiss plant-protection law. Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance Annex 2.5, Swiss PSMV (SR 916.161), and the UVEK ordinance on specialist permits for agricultural use (VFB-L, 24 Nov 2022, SR 814.812.34) apply. The Amt für Umwelt, Agriculture Department issues individual written special permits under the LBAV (LGBl. 2009 Nr. 264). Rules ban use on arable land 1 Nov to 15 Feb. The farm population is very small and the Swiss Fachbewilligung is held centrally. No candidate.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: The search returned no Liechtenstein sources, only German and Swiss municipal rules. Cemeteries are likely run by the 11 municipalities and funeral directors are few. No register or recurring report found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Itinerant trade: law of 26 Nov 2003 and ordinance of 13 Jan 2004 (LGBl. 2004 Nr. 12). The Amt für Volkswirtschaft issues an ID-card permit listing permitted goods, with a time restriction. Nothing found on currency exchange (Wechselstube) licensing. The permit holder count is tiny. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: No Liechtenstein-specific fuel-retailer licence found. Swiss rules apply by customs union: mineral-oil tax and CO2 levy (BAZG guideline 09), and the Swiss compulsory-stock regime (Carbura) for importers above the threshold. Station and heating-oil tank operators fall under the VWF water-protection ordinance (see candidate C1 and category 12). Only a handful of stations exist.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Cooperatives fall under the PGR (Personen- und Gesellschaftsrecht). From 1 Jan 2025 the amended Handelsregisterverordnung (Art. 92) and PGR (Art. 247, 1058a) require registration and an auditor for associations meeting certain conditions. Cooperatives are examined by the Amt für Justiz. The sector is small (Raiffeisen, Alp cooperatives). Weak candidate listed.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Liechtenstein is in the Swiss customs union, so Swiss customs rules apply. EUTR is applicable in the EEA. A source states EUDR application from 30 Dec 2026 for large and medium firms and 30 Jun 2027 for micro and small, but this is inconsistent across sources. Whether Liechtenstein has incorporated the EUDR into the EEA Agreement was not verified. No importer register found, and importers of forest-risk goods are few. Unverified.

result.reason: Duty is real. The PGR reform (LGBl. 2024 Nr. 370, in force 1 Jan 2025) requires registration of charitable associations, a domestic Repräsentanz, a member register kept in the country, and beneficial-owner entry. The Amt für Justiz can grant an exemption. The transition period ended 30 June 2026, and I found no extension. I could not open the Amt für Justiz leaflet (403), so I relied on search summaries. Penalties and annual recurring duties were not verified. No Liechtenstein-specific software was found; generic club software (ClubDesk, easyVerein) exists but does not do this job. Market size was not found. Only a minority of associations are caught, the duty is largely one-off, volunteer boards pay little, and fiduciaries serve the group. That makes it a weak recurring SaaS case.

Duty is real: Entsendegesetz (LGBl. 2000 Nr. 88, amended 2024) and Gewerbegesetz require prior online notification to the Amt für Volkswirtschaft. Trades need a confirmation before starting, renewed yearly. ZPK notification applies in sectors with a generally binding collective agreement. Foreign firms also need VAT registration. The search results show a free state online form and no third-party tool, but I only ran two searches. Penalty amounts, notification volumes and the form's usability were not checked (the PDF was unreadable, the IHK page returned 403). The market is tiny: Liechtenstein has about 40k residents. Buyers are scattered foreign trades, the duty is occasional and the state form is free. A done-for-you service might sell but would stay small. Whether third parties may file is unknown.

decisions.reason: Non-profit associations with commercial-register, member-list and VwbPG duties from 1 Jan 2025 (PGR reform) are a different buyer group than K01's TCSPs; related to K01.
Foreign small trades must notify the Amt für Volkswirtschaft before each job under Entsendegesetz Art. 6a; a recurring duty on small firms, new buyer and duty.
Small medical practices face a mandatory billing switch to TARDOC under the KVV amendment (LGBl. 2025 Nr. 553); a deadline makes many act at once and the duty falls on the clinics.
Real-estate brokers and dealers under SPG are small professional offices with an AML duty; different buyer group from K01's TCSPs (related K01). Unverified, so keep.
Same household-employer buyer and same monthly registration and payroll duty as K02; no new evidence to revive it.
Licensed weapons dealers and holders have recurring record-keeping duties under the Waffengesetz; small businesses in scope and unverified.

Same tank-owner buyer group and the same Amt für Umwelt tank-compliance duty. ALL7 comes first in the list, but GAPS1 is the better-specified version (VWF, 10-year inspection, Tankkontrollbuch), so keep GAPS1 and fold ALL7 into it.
Nurseries and day parents need Amt für Soziale Dienste approval and file KBBV reports; a small licensed-premises duty and in scope.
Small temp-staffing and placement agencies must hold a permit and deposit under the AVG and AVV and keep them current; in scope.
Small PV owners and landlords forming self-consumption communities have administrative duties under the Energieeffizienzgesetz; households and small firms, unverified.
Tank owners have recurring VWF inspections, leak-detector checks and a Tankkontrollbuch; small firms and households, new duty. It also absorbs ALL7.
Beekeepers must register apiaries, give advance notice of colony moves and keep a treatment journal; sole traders and hobbyists, new buyer group.
Same associations buyer group and same core duty (commercial-register registration and audit under the PGR changes from 1 Jan 2025); the co-op angle is a minor extension of ALL1.
